summary: This note is a short biography of Jessie Woodrow Wilson Sayre (1887–1933), a daughter of US President Woodrow Wilson and Ellen Louise Axson. It describes her as a political activist who worked for women's suffrage, social issues, and her father's League of Nations proposal, and who became a force in the Massachusetts Democratic Party.
one_line: Biographical note on Jessie Woodrow Wilson Sayre, daughter of President Woodrow Wilson and a political activist in women's suffrage and the Massachusetts Democratic Party.
key_facts: Jessie Woodrow Wilson Sayre was born on August 28, 1887.
Jessie Woodrow Wilson Sayre died on January 15, 1933.
Jessie Woodrow Wilson Sayre was a daughter of US President Woodrow Wilson.
Jessie Woodrow Wilson Sayre's mother was Ellen Louise Axson.
Jessie Woodrow Wilson Sayre was a political activist.
Jessie Woodrow Wilson Sayre worked vigorously for women's suffrage.
Jessie Woodrow Wilson Sayre worked on social issues.
Jessie Woodrow Wilson Sayre worked to promote her father's call for a League of Nations.
Jessie Woodrow Wilson Sayre emerged as a force in the Massachusetts Democratic Party.
